proposal.hypothesis: The stock PLA jaw faces are not parallel at wide openings and have low friction. Round objects wider than 40 mm get pushed out of the jaws, and the 514 g box slips during the last few mm of the lift.
proposal.rationale: All three failures stop the same way: stopped_by=slip, with pad_drop_t (3.46-4.46 s) showing the jaw pressure dropping under a constant command. They differ only in geometry. strawberry (width_mm=46.8) and racquetball (width_mm=55.5) are round and wider than the sphere grip limit of 40 mm. Their travel_reached (0.8435 and 0.5435 m against travel_required=0.03), contact_types=edge,pinch and peak_force of about 64-66 N mean the object was squeezed out between non-parallel faces and thrown, not lifted. The design notes say the stock faces are parallel only when closed, so wide objects are squeezed out. Tilting the pad (pad_angle_deg) makes the faces parallel at a wide opening, and a V-groove (groove_mm) centres the round objects. sugar_box (514 g) got to travel_reached=0.02447 of 0.03 before slipping, so the lift almost worked and failed on friction. A TPU skin raises friction from 0.45 to 0.9, which halves the squeeze needed to hold 5 N of weight. That is 3 edits, within the limit of max edits 3.
ruled_out: rung0: stopped_by=slip and pad_drop_t on every control, plus round objects wider than the 40 mm sphere grip (46.8 and 55.5 mm), point to a jaw geometry and friction limit. The grasp ranges (close, depth, side) that S1 already exhausted cannot change face angle or friction.
rung1: the only primitive that can lift (provides lifts=grasp) is grasp, alone or inside pick_up, so recomposing it keeps the same jaw contact that slips.
rung2: the rack is empty, so there is no existing tool to use or adapt.
rung3: accepted_contacts=pinch only, and none of the tool templates (pad, hook, knob_cup, soft_tip, slot_inserter, probe) gives a two-jaw pinch, so only the fingers can change the pinch surfaces.

proposal.hypothesis: Non-parallel stock faces at wide openings plus PLA friction of 0.45 cause the slip. Parallel TPU pads alone should hold all three objects without a groove.
proposal.rationale: This is a fallback in case the V-groove reduces flat-face contact on sugar_box (width_mm=92.2, a box face). It keeps the two changes the evidence supports most strongly. pad_angle_deg addresses the squeeze-out seen in strawberry and racquetball: travel_reached far beyond 0.03, peak_force of about 64-66 N, contact_types including edge. pad_tpu_mm addresses the friction-limited slip of the 514 g box, which reached travel_reached=0.02447 of 0.03 before stopped_by=slip at pad_drop_t=3.46.
ruled_out: rung0: every control fails by stopped_by=slip with a pad pressure drop (pad_drop_t), which is a face-angle and friction limit that the grasp parameter ranges cannot reach.
rung1: grasp is the only lifting primitive, so any recomposed program uses the same slipping jaw contact.
rung2: the rack is empty, so there is no library tool to use.
rung3: accepted_contacts=pinch, and no tool template provides a two-jaw pinch.
